2. The present application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Case No. 2162 of 2023, arising out of case crime no. 0273 of 2020, (State v. Rupa Mishra), under Sections 323, 347, 387, 449, 506, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 474, 120-B IPC and Section 66-C, 66-D Indian Information Technology Act, P.S. Gopiganj, District Sant Ravidas Nagar (Bhadohi), pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhadohi and to quash the charge-sheet dated 09.12.2022 as well as cognizance/summoning order dated 31.01.2023 passed in the aforesaid case.

sentences.text:
It has been argued by learned senior counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and she is not named in the first information report, which was lodged against co-accused Vijay Mishra,
Ramlali Mishra and Vishnu Mishra.
During investigation, no evidence has been collected against the applicant and despite that applicant was made an accused.
The informant did not name the applicant in his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Other witnesses, including family members of informant also did not name the applicant in their statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
The statement of informant under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was also recorded but the applicant was not named therein.

After investigation, charge-sheet was submitted against co-accused Vijay Mishra,
and Ramlali Mishra, who are father-in-law and mother-in-law of applicant.

Thereafter on 25.02.2022 another charge-sheet was submitted against applicant's husband, namely, Vishnu Mishra but the Investigating Officer kept the investigation open against applicant and name of the applicant has been figured for the first time in that charge-sheet.
Applicant has already been granted anticipatory bail.

It was further submitted that on 09.12.2022, the Investigating Officer has filed charge-sheet against the applicant under Sections 323, 347, 387, 449, 506, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471,
474, 120-B IPC and Section 66-C, 66-D of Indian Information Technology Act but neither any overt act has been attributed to the applicant nor any specific role has been assigned to her.
The prosecution story is false and concocted and that as the applicant belongs to a political family and her father-in-law has been M.L.A. for several times, thus, this case is politically motivated.
Even otherwise the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature, which has been given criminal colour.

It was submitted that M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari is a partnership firm and that applicant's mother-in-law, namely, Smt. Ramlali Mishra, along with Krishna Mohan Tiwari and one Ashok Shukla are partners in the said partnership firm and that there is an arbitration clause that in case of any dispute, the matter shall be referred to the Arbitration.
The informant in order to grab the partnership business has lodged the FIR of this case.

Noticing the illegal acts of informant, the other partners, namely, Smt. Ramlali Mishra and Ashok Shukla have also filed a case under Section 9 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act for referring the matter to the Arbitration.

The District Judge,
Bhadohi, while partly allowing the application under Section 9 of the said Act, has held that it is a partnership firm and in that connection the matter is pending in arbitration appeal before this Court, wherein, an interim order has been passed with regard to the properties of the firm, directing the informant to prepare separate account with regard to sale and purchase of partnership firm's property.

The partners of the firm have also preferred a petition under Section 11 of Arbitration Act for appointment of Arbitrator and by order dated 16.09.2022 a retired Judge of Hon'ble Supreme Court was appointed as Arbitrator.

Learned senior counsel has referred statements of witnesses,
recorded during investigation, and submitted that dispute between the parties is civil in nature and the same has been given criminal colour so that the properties of partnership firm may be grabbed.
Informant has admitted the partnership bank account and that bank account is still operating and thereby informant is usurping this partnership bank account for his personal benefits.
Further, the informant has immovable properties of partnership firm and he did not prepare any separate account, as directed by this Court.

Informant has also withdrawn an amount of Rs. 14 crores from the partnership bank account and that Bank officers are in hand and glove with informant and they are not allowing other partners to operate partnership bank account.
The FIR of this case has been lodged by the informant for blackmailing and to escape his liability of paying the amount illegally withdrawn by the informant.
The details of certain cheques and transactions were also referred and it was submitted that there is no credible evidence against the applicant.

sentences.text: Learned senior counsel further submitted that there is no allegation against the applicant regarding taking away, grabbing of any property or executing sale deeds of any immovable properties/lands in favour of family members of applicant.
No details of the disputed land had been given in the statements of witnesses.
No specific sale-deed or date or time or any instance of alienation of land has been given and even the names of seller and purchaser have not been mentioned.
In fact Sushila Devi herself has admitted that she has given land to her daughter Pushpalata, who is sister of informant.
Informant has civil dispute with his family members and that a partition case was also pending among them.
Several other proceedings among family members were also referred.

It is further submitted that informant and applicant's father-in-law are co-accused in CC No. 111/02 PS Gopiganj & CC No. 147/02 Gopiganj and one more case under the Mines And Mineral Act was also registered against them in the year 2017.

Refereeing to facts of the matter, it was submitted that till August, 2020 relation of informant and applicant's family were very cordial until dishonesty erupted in mind of informant and he lodged this frivolous FIR to grab the business.

It was submitted that applicant's father-in-law was arrested on 14.08.2020 and thereafter several FIRs have been lodged against the family members of applicant, the details of which have been mentioned in the affidavit filed in support of the application.

It was also pointed out that informant has filed an affidavit dated 26.10.2020 before the Investigating Officer in FIR no.
273 of 2020, police station Gopiganj, in which he has stated that he has no concern with the partnership bank account of SBI, Bhadohi branch but now he is claiming the properties/vehicles,
which were purchased by the partnership firm bank account.

5. It is further submitted that there is no allegation in the FIR or in the statements of witnesses,
against the applicant and she has been made an accused without there being any credible evidence against her.
The present case is nothing but politically motivated.
Merely because the applicant was shown partner in the firm, she cannot be held liable for the offences in question.
In criminal law a person cannot be held vicarious liable.

Learned senior advocate has also referred the case of Sunita Palita & Ors. v. M/s Panchami Stone Quarry, 2022 (10) SCC 152 and submitted that merely because applicant is partner in the partnership firm, no prima facie case is made out against the applicant,
particularly, when there is no allegation in the FIR against her and and that no specific allegation was made by any witness against her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned senior advocate submitted that in view of above-stated facts and circumstances of the case, the impugned charge-sheet and proceedings are nothing but abuse of the process of law and the same are liable to be quashed.
Charge-sheet submitted against the applicant was also referred and it was submitted that charge-sheet shows that no credible evidence has been collected against the applicant.

6. Sri Abhishek Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the informant and Sri M.C. Chaturvedi, learned Additional Advocate General have opposed the application and argued that during investigation,
evidence has been collected which indicates that applicant was involved in this case.

During investigation, it was found that the applicant is director in the firms of accused persons, namely, Nav Nirman Infra Heights & Movers Pvt. Ltd., VSP STARR Royalty Pvt. Ltd., Lalira Construction Pvt.
Ltd., Lalira Buildcon Pvt. Ltd. and Lalira Jewelers Pvt. Ltd. and that she was actively dealing with the business and transactions of the said firms.

sentences.text: It was shown that on 17.09.2015 Rs. 1 lac and on 08.01.2016 Rs. 1.5 lacs were transferred into the account of applicant from the disputed account and besides that funds were transferred into the accounts of the firms/company, of which the applicant is director/partner.
These firms are directly connected with the firm and transactions of the firm in dispute.
The forged pan card of informant was used in opening of one of the bank account.
It is further pointed out that in the term loan account of the informant, co-accused Vijay Mishra, Vishnu Mishra and applicant are guarantors.

Referring to case diary, it was submitted that during investigation, it was found that the accused persons were indulging in usurping property of others by taking political advantage and they have made several firms and that a false pan number has been shown in the account of informant and informant has told that the said pan card is not belong to him.
It was also pointed out that the vehicles of informant were used by co-accused Vishnu Mishra and applicant in their firm Nav Nirman Infra Heights & Movers Pvt. Ltd.

sentences.text: I have considered the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. The legal position on the issue of quashing of criminal proceedings is well-settled that the jurisdiction to quash a complaint, FIR or a charge-sheet should be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.

However, where the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and material on record even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused, the charge-sheet may be quashed in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

In well celebrated judgement reported in AIR 1992 SC 605 State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal, Supreme Court has carved out certain guidelines, wherein FIR or proceedings may be quashed but cautioned that the power to quash FIR or proceedings should be exercised sparingly and that too in the rarest of rare cases.
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant matter, the informant Krishna Mohan Tiwari has lodged the FIR against co-accused Vijay Mishra, Ramlali Mishra and Vishnu Mishra, alleging that the said accused persons are doing their political and economical activities from the building of informant and they have forcibly taken possession over there.

The informant was doing his business by his name M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari but the said accused persons have taken over the business of said firm in their names and huge amount was transferred from the firm to co-accused Ramlali Mishra and Vishnu Mishra and that they are exploiting the informant and his family members and they used to threat him.
After forging a Will, they were pressurizing the informant to transfer his property in the name of Vishnu Mishra and when informant refused, he was being threatened.

Applicant is not named in the FIR,
however, it appears that during investigation, it was found that applicant, who is wife of co-accused Vishnu Mishra, was director in the several firms of the accused persons and as per prosecution,
several properties of the informant's firm were misappropriated and amounts were illegally withdrawn and some amount was transferred in the account of applicant and the firms, of which applicant is one of the partner.

The applicant has been charge-sheeted under Sections 323, 347, 387,
449, 506, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 474, IPC and Section 66-C, 66-D of Indian Information Technology Act with the aid of Section 120-B IPC.

Rupa Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191642311/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicant(s) call for determination on questions of fact which may be adequately adjudicated upon only by the trial court and even the submissions made on points of law can also be more appropriately gone into only by the trial court.
Adjudication of questions of facts and appreciation of evidence or examining the reliability and credibility of the version, does not fall within the arena of jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

In view of the material on record it can also not be held that the impugned criminal proceeding are manifestly attended with mala fide and maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge.

11. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the case diary and the material collected during investigation, it cannot be said that no prima facie case is made out against the applicant.

The contentions raised by learned senior counsel on behalf of the applicant requires determination on questions of fact, which is not permissible in the proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
12.

After considering arguments raised by the learned counsel for parties and perusing the impugned charge-sheet and the materials in support of the same, this Court does not find it to be a case which can be determined or gone into in an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
This Court cannot hold a parallel trial in an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

Considering material on record and position of settled law as laid down in the case of R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, A.I.R.
1960 S.C. 866, State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 426, State of Bihar Vs. P.P.Sharma,
1992 SCC (Cr.) 192 and Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs. Mohd. Saraful Haq and another 2005 SCC (Cr.) 283 and Rajeev Kourav vs. Bhaisahab & Ors., (2020)3 SCC 317, no case for quashing of impugned proceedings/charge-sheet and cognizance order is made out.

The instant application lacks merit and it is, accordingly,
dismissed.
